skill.name: caveman-review
skill.description: Ultra-compressed code review comments. Cuts noise from PR feedback while preserving the actionable signal. Each comment is one line: location, problem, fix. Use when user says "review this PR", "code review", "review the diff", "/review", or invokes /caveman-review. Auto-triggers when reviewing pull requests.

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code examples and normal review terminology in SKILL.md. The skill is prose-only guidance for formatting code review comments; no executable commands, network behavior, prompt injection, or data access intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: - `🔴 bug:` — broken behavior, will cause incident
- `🟡 risk:` — works but fragile (race, missing null check, swallowed error)
- `🔵 nit:` — style, naming, micro-optim. Author can ignore
- `❓ q:` — genuine question, not a suggestion
- "This is just a suggestion but..." — use `nit:` instead
✅ `L42: 🔴 bug: user can be null after .find(). Add guard before .email.`
✅ `L88-140: 🔵 nit: 50-line fn does 4 things. Extract validate/normalize/persist.`

content.user_title: Write Concise Pull Request Review Comments
content.value_statement: Pull request reviews often become too wordy for quick action. This skill formats feedback as concise, paste-ready comments with location, problem, and fix.
actual_capabilities: Turns review feedback into one-line comments with location, problem, and fix.
Applies optional severity prefixes for bugs, risks, nits, and questions.
Removes hedging, praise, and repeated explanations from review comments.
Keeps exact line numbers and symbol names in feedback.
Switches to fuller explanation for security, architecture, or onboarding contexts.
limitations: Does not run tests, linters, or static analysis tools.
Does not write code fixes or modify repository files.
Does not approve or request changes on pull requests.
Needs accurate diff context to produce reliable line references.

use_cases.title: Condense PR Feedback
use_cases.description: Convert long draft feedback into paste-ready comments that identify line, issue, and fix.

use_cases.title: Focus Large Reviews
use_cases.description: Keep review discussions focused during large diffs by separating bugs, risks, nits, and questions.

use_cases.title: Reply to Contributors
use_cases.description: Respond to contributor pull requests with concise comments while preserving useful guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this diff with caveman-review. Return one-line comments with location, problem, and fix.

prompt_templates.title: Condense Draft Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite my draft PR comments in caveman-review style. Keep facts, remove hedging, and preserve line references.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Mixed Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this multi-file diff. Prefix each item as bug, risk, nit, or question when helpful. Use file and line references.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Review Exceptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this security-sensitive change. Use normal paragraphs for serious security or architecture findings, then use terse comments for routine items.

output_examples.input: Long comment about a missing guard before reading a user email on line 42.
output_examples.output: Line 42: bug: user may be missing. Add a guard before reading the email field.

output_examples.input: Review note asking whether retry handling is needed after rate limits.
output_examples.output: Line 23: risk: rate limits fail once. Add bounded retry handling.

output_examples.input: Draft feedback says one large function should be easier to read.
output_examples.output: Lines 88-140: nit: function has four jobs. Extract validation, normalization, and persistence steps.

best_practices: Provide the diff and enough surrounding context for accurate line references.
Use normal mode for security findings, architecture decisions, and new contributor coaching.
Ask for severity prefixes when reviewing mixed issues in one pull request.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to approve or reject a pull request for you.
Do not expect it to run tests, linters, or static analysis tools.
Do not force terse output when a finding needs a detailed explanation.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It formats code review feedback into concise comments with a line reference, problem, and fix.

faq.question: Which tools support it?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as listed by the skill metadata.

faq.question: Does it execute commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is prose guidance for review comments and does not instruct command execution.

faq.question: Can it review security bugs?
faq.answer: Yes, but it tells the assistant to use fuller explanations for serious security findings.

faq.question: Will it change code?
faq.answer: No. It formats review comments and does not apply fixes.

faq.question: How do I stop terse mode?
faq.answer: Use stop caveman-review or normal mode to request a verbose review style.
